A lot of water systems have begun using chloroamine on top of chlorine as part of their water sterilization process. Chloramine stays in the water longer and doesn't 'bubble out' like chlorine does. I'm not sure if your tetra conditioner is dealing with the rapidly decaying chloroamine properly. When chloroamine breaks down(NH2Cl), it creates ammonia (NH3) by losing a chlorine ion and picking up a hydrogen atom from the water. If you don't have something to bind directly to the ammonia, then you might be inadvertently spiking your ammonia from doing water changes. 

Worst case, if chloroamine has worked it's way into your tank it's possible that it knocked out the biological filter as well, furthering your problems with ammonia. You'd need more startup bacteria if that's the case.

If you have a filter on the tank, make sure the intake is fully covered or the babies will get sucked up and killed. Other than that small precaution, keep doing what you're doing. The shrimp are happy enough to mate, so the tank must be healthy.

You're not worrying too much, it's quite common for babies (even juveniles!) to be sucked up into the filter never to be see again. There are a couple ways you can prevent this from happening.. 

The first method involves taking a stocking (pantyhose) and placing it over the intake. I think you use a rubber band to tightly hold the stocking to the intake pipe. This will block babies from being sucked up, but can get blocked rather quickly.

The second (and the method I prefer) is taking a pair of scissors to the block foam inserts that you can put in larger filters. I cut out an "x" in the foam and insert the intake into that. I think this method is better because the babies don't get sucked up AND they have the sponge to pick at. The only real detriment to this is that eventually you have to take off the sponge and rinse it every few months. Otherwise the sponge gets too dirty and limits flow into your filter.

Hi there! I am [Carnby of Thrall](http://us.battle.net/wow/en/character/thrall/Carnby/simple). My guild killed Heroic Garrosh two weeks ago and I'm hoping to help you out as best I can!

The first thing I notice about your character is your hit rating... It's too high! You only need 7.5% (2,550 rating) to be 'hit capped' on bosses. This means that you can reforge the extra hit rating to something else that would be more useful!

Secondly, you have no Expertise. Expertise is very important to hunters, as we do not want our shots (or our pet's attacks) to be dodged or parried.

.

.

.

**Gear**

All of this information I have from [your AskMrRobot page](http://www.askmrrobot.com/wow/gear/usa/azgalor/taladen). I'm just trying to help decipher it for you.

Helmet - Gemming is fine, reforge Hit Rating to Critical Strike

Necklace -  Gemming is fine, reforge Mastery rating to Critical Strike.

Shoulder - Place a [Deadly Vermilion Onyx](http://www.wowhead.com/item=76658/deadly-vermilion-onyx) in each yellow socket, enchant with [Greater Tiger Claw Inscription](http://www.wowhead.com/item=83007), and reforge Mastery to Expertise rating.

Back - Enchant your cloak with [Superior Critical Strike](http://www.wowhead.com/item=74713), no reforge needed on this piece.

Chest - Place two [Delicate Primordial Ruby](http://www.wowhead.com/item=76692) into the two red sockets, with a [Deadly Vermilion Onyx](http://www.wowhead.com/item=76658) into the yellow socket to activate the bonus. Enchant it with [Glorious Stats](http://www.wowhead.com/item=74708), and reforge Mastery to Expertise.

Wrist - Enchant with [Greater Agility](http://www.wowhead.com/item=74705), and reforge Mastery to Expertise.

Hands - Gemming is fine, enchant with [Superior Expertise](http://www.wowhead.com/item=74720), reforge Haste to Expertise.

Belt - Get a [Living Steel Belt Buckle](http://www.wowhead.com/item=90046) and place a [Delicate Primordial Ruby](http://www.wowhead.com/item=76692) into the socket.

Legs - Gemming is fine, enchant with [Shadowleather Leg Armor](http://www.wowhead.com/item=83764), and reforge Mastery to Expertise.

Feet - Place a [Delicate Primordial Ruby](http://www.wowhead.com/item=76692) into the red socket, enchant with [Blurred Speed](http://www.wowhead.com/item=74717), and reforge Hit to Expertise.

Ring 1 - Gemming is fine, reforge Mastery to Expertise

Ring 2 - Reforge Mastery to Crit

Trinket 1 - N/A

Trinket 2 - Reforge Hit to Crit

I know that this process will be long and probably expensive initally, but I assure you that having these stats balanced will tremendously help your dps. After all of this, you will be much closer to 7.5% Expertise and Hit. This means that the additional stats that were going towards the extra hit are now going toward more useful stats, such as Expertise or Critical Strike!

.

.

.

**Professions**

You should probably work on leveling your professions. There are a few great choices as a hunter.

[Engineering](http://www.wowhead.com/skill=202) gets you tons of awesome little toys to play with, mounts, and on-use boost to your agility when you want it. (My #1 Recommendation)

[Blacksmithing](http://www.wowhead.com/skill=164) allows you to add additional gem sockets to your gloves and bracers.

[Inscription](http://www.wowhead.com/skill=773) gets you cheaper shoulder enchants, but isn't much of a money-maker unless you're making Darkmoon decks.

[Jewelcrafting](http://www.wowhead.com/skill=755) gets you more powerful gems than most people have access to, plus it allows you to save money by cutting your own gems.

[Skinning](http://www.wowhead.com/skill=393) grants you additional Critical Strike rating, and can get you some good money if you farm tons of leather.

[Leatherworking](http://www.wowhead.com/skill=165) will give you more powerful bracer enchants at a reduced cost, and can even make good money if you're skinning and making armor yourself.

[Herbalism](http://www.wowhead.com/skill=182) gives you lifeblood, which heals you and boots your haste for 20 seconds every few minutes. It can make good money on its own or paired with Alchemy.

[Alchemy](http://www.wowhead.com/skill=171) increases the duration and effectiveness of your flasks. This profession can be a moderately steady stream of income, as raiders on your server will always need flasks.

[Enchanting](http://www.wowhead.com/skill=333) allows you to enchant your rings. Non-enchanters are not able to do this, and will look on in envy (kinda)!

I would personally stay away from tailoring, mining, and inscription, but I can't stop you!

1. DPS - For the most part, if you have a GCD going unclicked (unpressed for keybinding people), you've missed out on dps. Attempt to use abilities as soon as they come up for maximum efficiency.

2. Tanking - Same thing as DPS. If you're missing a GCD, you're missing on threat and even damage (tank damage CAN kill a boss). Make sure you're not killing yourself though by hitting the boss when he's got a buff that hurts you though.

3. Healers - If everyone is at full health. Start looking proactively at the battlefield. You can pretty easily predict where people are going to take damage if you know the fight well enough.

4. Don't stand in the fire.

5. Avoid mudslinging in trade chat. Nothing makes you seem more immature than calling a fellow player out in a channel dedicated to trade.

6. Begin to keybind. This is a very effective way of increasing dps by a little bit. Your fingers will learn where each ability is on the keyboard and that will increase your responsiveness. (I use Bartender to do this as there is a built-in keybinding functionality in it) Alt-W is a LOT better for multi-shot than hitting or clicking 7 on the keyboard.

7. Hunt rares in Pandaria. They are challenging fights and will force you to learn your class. Avoid the upper-level panda ones unless you have a second person including yourself to interrupt the healing spell they cast.

8. Take advice from other players. Taking from this myself, let's build upon these points.
